review_reference: Owner, 2026-11-14, during the outreach: "we should collect genotype and blood group" (both optional; a screening still saves without them). NOT SIGNED: to be signed by the owner before the branch is merged, so the merge release applies 0122 (plan, dry run, apply) before it rolls outreach-api. Declares 0122 alone: production has 0120 and 0121 applied (release run 43521287214 deployed 4880ee42 with database-migration selected and succeeded at 23:04 UTC on 2026-11-13; a deploy succeeds only when no migration is left pending). The number 0122 is also used by origin/claude/fervent-galileo-datz4t-prescription-details (0122_prescription_dispensing_details.sql) and origin/pr222 (0122_outreach_campaign_admins.sql): whichever releases second is renumbered. Exposure (decision pending with the owner): genotype and blood group are answered only by the per-registration screening read and save, each with its own audit row; the registration list, read, create and link answers and the website export carry neither.
evidence: Migration 0122_outreach_screening_blood.sql (placeholder; releases right after 0121). runtime-grants.sql is unchanged. WHAT IT DOES: outreach.registration_screenings (0118) gains two nullable text columns with no default: genotype (CHECK registration_screenings_genotype_check: 'AA','AS','AC','SS','SC','CC','unknown') and blood_group (CHECK registration_screenings_blood_group_check: 'A+','A-','B+','B-','AB+','AB-','O+','O-','unknown'), the same codes as outreach-api and the website. The CHECKs are added NOT VALID, then validated. Nothing else changes: 0118's trigger never names the clinical columns, so its version, facility, actor, suspension and redaction rules cover the new columns; row-level security, policies and the table grant (select, insert, update to hid_outreach_runtime) are per table; a redaction deletes the whole screening row; audit rows stay ids only. PRECONDITIONS (55000, nothing applied): 0118 applied, neither column present. POST-CHECKS: both columns nullable text with no default, both CHECKs validated, no hid_* runtime role may DELETE a screening. LOCKS: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on outreach.registration_screenings. It waits up to 5 seconds for the lock without blocking anyone (NOWAIT every 10 ms, then 55P03 and nothing applied); once it has the lock it holds it for milliseconds to commit (no row is rewritten; the validation reads the screening rows once, every new value being null). The release takes it twice: dry run (rolled back), then apply. SERVICES: today's outreach-api reads with select * and ignores the new columns, its insert leaves them null, and its update names its own columns, so it keeps a recorded genotype and blood group. The new outreach-api runs on a database with or without 0122: it learns from each screening select * whether the two columns exist and names them only then (accepts [] and a 409 OUTREACH_SCREENING_FIELDS_NOT_TAKEN for a value before 0122); its registration list, read, create and link answers name no 0122 column and carry no genotype or blood group, only hasScreening and hasRecordedChecks (false for a screening saved with nothing filled in). An update that leaves genotype or bloodGroup out keeps it; null clears it (API behaviour). Proven on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 with fictional data: the new build on a 0121 database read (accepts []), saved an empty first screening (hasScreening true, hasRecordedChecks false), refused a genotype value with 409, ignored null, and listed with no genotype key; 0122 was then applied to that database holding the screening; the new build answered accepts both, set AS and O-, kept them when left out, and listed hasRecordedChecks true for a screening holding only a genotype or only a medicine and false for one holding nothing, with no genotype key on any registration. Earlier on this branch: today's outreach-api build read, updated and listed before and after 0122 and kept a genotype and blood group the new build recorded. All 94 database suites pass on 0001-0122, including outreach-screening.integration.sql with 40 0122 cases (78 in all). ROLLBACK: a later migration dropping the two columns, which permanently deletes every recorded genotype and blood group. The new outreach-api needs no rollback first (its next screening read sees the columns gone).
